title: applied-ml experiment scratchpad - 2026-03-05 (Jamie)
content:
Date: 2026-03-05
Owner: Jamie Chen (applied-ml)

Goal for today:
- Triage weird quality regression after moving to quant4-int8 on redwood-v1-small.
- Run focused eval on prompt set A/B and sanity-check generation latencies.
- Tune batching + KV cache policy for chat use-case.

Quick TODO:
- [ ] Re-run eval with deterministic seeds (seed=42) across quant variants (fp16, int8, quant4)
- [ ] Capture per-token latency histogram (p50/p95/p99) for short (32), med (128), long (512) seq lengths
- [ ] Check KV cache warmup behavior after rolling restart (RGW-2345)
- [ ] Post initial findings to #applied-ml and link to PR

Experiment log (runs):
1) run: eval-prompt-A_fp16
- model: redwood-v1-small (fp16)
- prompt-set: prompt-A (customer-support style, 120 prompts)
- batch: 8, max_new_tokens: 128, temp: 0.0
- metrics: exact-match 0.62, rouge-L 0.71, avg latency per request 210ms (tokens/sec 320)
- notes: baseline, looks good and consistent with earlier runs (2026-02-27)

2) run: eval-prompt-A_quant4
- model: redwood-v1-small-quant4
- same prompts and config
- metrics: exact-match 0.55, rouge-L 0.66, avg latency per request 180ms (tokens/sec 380)
- notes: faster but drop in fidelity on tail cases (tables, numeric extraction). Possible quantization-induced token mispredictions.

3) run: eval-prompt-B_fp16 (chatty instruction-style prompts)
- metrics: BLEU-ish heur 0.48, avg latency 230ms

4) run: eval-prompt-B_quant4
- metrics: BLEU-ish heur 0.40, avg latency 190ms
- notes: hallucination increase for prompts that require step-by-step reasoning. Suspect rounding error in topk probabilities.

Initial hypothesis:
- Quant4 gives ~15-20% throughput improvement but degrades quality on specific prompt archetypes (tabular extraction, multi-step reasoning).
- Potential causes: post-quantization softmax sharpness changes; kernel selection fallback rounding; KV cache precision loss accumulating on long contexts.

Immediate tests to run:
- Compare logits distribution (fp16 vs quant4) for failure examples (generate top-10 logit diffs)
- Run calibration pass: scaled-activation calibration (per-layer) and re-evaluate on failing cases
- Try hybrid setup: key/query in fp16, rest quant4 (if runtime supports)

Commands/notes (local dev machine):
- eval script: ./tools/run_eval.sh --model redwood-v1-small --quant quant4 --prompts data/prompt-set-A.json --batch 8 --seed 42 --out out/quant4-run.json
- perf capture: perf-tool --target pid --out perf/quant4-profile.txt

Perf snapshots (from quick runs):
- fp16: p50=180ms p95=320ms p99=520ms (32-token new: p50=60ms)
- quant4: p50=150ms p95=260ms p99=430ms
- memory: fp16 peak 9.2GB, quant4 peak 6.8GB

Observations/details:
- One failing prompt (id: A_087): requires extracting two dates from a paragraph. fp16 returns exact dates, quant4 returns approximate phrasing ("early March").
- Token-level diff shows mispredictions at position 7-9 where quant4 top-1 token diverges. Logit histogram shows decreased margin between top-1 and top-2 after quantization.
- Warmup: after process start, first 50 requests show slightly higher latencies; KV cache seems to reduce p50 by ~25ms after warmup. After rolling restart, clients see a small spike; need smoother draining. Filing RGW-2345 for canary restart policy.

Notes to include in write-up:
- Performance gains are attractive for Dedicated where cost per token matters, but quality regression on critical prompt archetypes may prevent wholesale switch. Recommend per-route quantization policy (route-level config in console).
- Suggest adding a small eval gate in CI: run a 50-prompt smoke on important prompt sets when adding quantized binaries. Fail on >5% drop in exact-match vs baseline.

Follow-ups / Action items:
- [Asha] run logits diff tool and produce plots for failing prompts (due 2026-03-06)
- [Miguel] check runtime kernel fallback logs for quant4 runs (collect at /tmp/quant4-kernel-logs)
- [Jamie] implement hybrid key/query fp16 config and run targeted eval (in-progress)
- Create PR describing observed regression and recommended per-route quant policy (link to PR when ready)

Random notes / thoughts:
- Could try per-channel symmetric quantization for attention weights instead of per-tensor to preserve relative logits? Need to discuss with infra/release engineering.
- If regression is only on a small subset, we can surface a flag in Console: "optimize-for-cost" that applies aggressive quant for low-priority routes.

Links / references:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-ALGO-23456 (quantization notes)
- Jira: RGW-2345 (restart policy + warmup)
- PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-serving/pull/512

Notes-to-self:
- Keep experiment IDs consistent (date + short name)
- Save seed and run configs in out/ as json for reproducibility

End of scratchpad for 2026-03-05.
